comments.author: Glawen
comments.story: Latest 737 Max Fault That Alarmed Test Pilots Rooted in Software
comments.why: Shows how the landing gear was modified for height
comments.text: Because you then need longer and heavier landing gear, which you need to fit somewhere in the plane as they retract. This is a ripple effect where you probably need to redesign the complete airframe, from fuselage to the wings. They actually cleverly modified the landing gear to gain a bit of heigth, but it was not enough: [VIDEO]

comments.author: JorgeGT
comments.story: A 50-year-old design came back to haunt Boeing with its troubled 737 Max jet
comments.why: Boeing engineer explains commonality constraint on landing gear
comments.text: Here's Gary Hamatani, chief project engineer for Boeing's 737 MAX program, explaining that they needed the main landing gear to fit the existing wheel wells: [VIDEO] I find it very illustrative, as it contains the keywords that are at issue here: "we wanted to preserve commonality", "from a pilot's perspective there's absolutely nothing different", etc.
